title: Technical analysis basics
objectives: Read trends, support/resistance, moving averages and RSI.
Explain the limits of technical analysis.
body_md:
Technical analysis studies **price and volume** to read trends.

## Core ideas

- **Dow theory:** markets move in primary, secondary and minor trends; averages confirm each other.
- **Support** is a price floor; **resistance** is a ceiling. A breakout on high volume is stronger.
- **Moving averages:** the 50-day and 200-day are common. A *golden cross* (50 crosses above 200) is bullish; a *death cross* is bearish.
- **RSI** (usually 14 periods): above 70 suggests overbought, below 30 oversold.
- **MACD:** difference of two moving averages with a signal line.
- **Candlesticks:** a hammer after a fall hints at reversal; a doji shows indecision.
- **Volume** should confirm the move.

## Limits

| Issue | Note |
|---|---|
| Subjective | Two analysts can read one chart differently |
| Weak-form efficiency | If past prices carry no edge, patterns may fail |
| Lagging | Most indicators follow price |

> **Exam tip:** Know the numeric thresholds: RSI 70 and 30.
example: A stock rises to ₹500 three times and falls back. ₹500 is resistance. A close above ₹510 on double the usual volume is a confirmed breakout.
